chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated that from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Mubarak, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd Allah ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir and Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asked us about a man who is obligated to fast two consecutive months, but he is unable to fast and is unable to pay the fidya (compensation). He said: 'Let him fast eighteen days: for every ten days, three days.'
ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for someone who cannot fast two consecutive months and cannot pay fidya?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfarayini’s chain in al-Istibsar details the graduated compensation (kaffarah) for breaking the Ramadan fast, specifically addressing the scenario where one is unable to fast the full two consecutive months or pay the fidya. It prescribes fasting eighteen days, structured as three days for every ten days of the missed obligation, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of proportional expiation based on capacity. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia fiqh to accommodate varying degrees of inability, ensuring the spiritual debt is cleared through manageable acts of worship.
